title: Can’t See the Forest for the Trees

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Can’t See the Forest for the Trees begins with AI editing that weakened its argument.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The sentences remained plausible while urgency, uncertainty, and responsibility became harder to see.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It connects that experience with institutions that improve local details while losing the larger problem.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its personal inquiry links technological progress with dependence, blind spots, and possible correction.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers are invited to examine a measured optimism that keeps difficult consequences in view.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The author describes AI revisions that preserved plausibility while softening the point he needed expressed.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: His concern was not simply whether individual sentences remained correct.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book contrasts a fundamental research uncertainty with its softer description as manageable risk.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That experience becomes an entry into a larger problem of apparently reasonable simplification.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A local improvement can make the whole account less faithful to what matters.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The inquiry moves from individual blind spots toward power, markets, attention, and institutional dependence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Imagine a backup service that looks wasteful during quarters when nothing breaks.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The author also examines the limits of his own entrepreneurial and technological perspective.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This personal position gives the argument stakes without making it an established theory of everything.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book keeps asking which connections disappear when each participant follows a narrower picture.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with the author's editing experience before following its links to larger systems.
